t: You're at Moorfields, which today is built over but was once an open space just outside London's northern wall, near Moorgate. It was known for being marshy. The wall acted as a dam, and held back the flow of the River Walbrook and its tributaries. Daniel Defoe died here. He was the writer, journalist, merchant and spy who gave us Robinson Crusoe in 1719, and he is seen as one of the earliest champions of the English novel.
